title: Friday the 13th: Why Do So Many People Fear This Day?
summary:
Friday, November 13, 2026, is the third and last Friday the 13th of this year.

For most people, it is just the start of the weekend. But millions of people feel it is the unluckiest day of the year. Some people fear it so much that the fear has a long name: paraskevidekatriaphobia. No one knows for sure how the fear began. Professor Thomas Fernsler of the University of Delaware says 13 has a bad name because it comes right after 12. People see 12 as a full, tidy number. Folklore historian Donald Dossey says the fear may come from an old Norse myth. Twelve gods were at dinner when Loki, the god of mischief, tricked Hodr, the blind god of darkness, into killing Baldr, the god of joy and light. The Bible says Jesus was crucified on a Friday, soon after the Last Supper, which had 13 people. That day, American businesses may lose as much as $900 million, but a 2008 study in the Netherlands found fewer car accidents than on other Fridays.
why_it_matters: Knowing where the fear of Friday the 13th comes from can help you decide for yourself whether to worry about the date or just enjoy the start of your weekend.
